definitions.corridor: top 0.1 of active directed ISL links ranked by served rate in the eval window
definitions.delta: delta_r = (bits wrongly routed into r - bits that should have entered r but went elsewhere)/window [bit/s]; sum_r delta_r = 0
definitions.epsilon: epsilon_r = mu_r - served_bits_r/window; mu_r = link rate_bps; clipped exactly per window from link_service_windows (stage=isl)
definitions.epsilon_caveat: served <= rate*window always holds, so epsilon >= 0 by construction; epsilon == 0 means saturated in that window (z = inf). Offered load from queue_enter arrivals is reported separately because it CAN exceed mu.
definitions.flip: truth-substituted same-decision re-ranking (same rule as sq_policy_analyze.py); geometry has no state term -> flip = 0 by construction
definitions.flip_rate: flips / multi-candidate scored forward decisions inside the window
definitions.persistence_stream: same-(sat,dst) decision stream; dst and bits are joined from trace.jsonl.gz by pid because load_calibration's decision projection drops dst (a decision-row dst would silently degrade this to per-sat)
definitions.tau_error: duration of a same-sign |delta_r| > frac*mu run per resource (0.5 s bins, censored at window edges)
definitions.tau_relax: time from a queue peak to 50% of the peak, and back into the p10-p90 band of the preceding 2 s
definitions.z: z = |delta_r| / epsilon_r, evaluated on the 0.5 s bin containing the decision; non-flips carry no delta and are a separate contrast row
definitions.z_caveat: delta_r and lambda_r are on different accounting bases: lambda_r counts bits actually served (misrouted bits included), delta_r is a counterfactual bookkeeping swing. z is therefore a NORMALISED BIAS MAGNITUDE (bias relative to residual capacity), not a load-triggered overload indicator; z >= 1 says the swing is comparable to or larger than the link's spare capacity in that bin, so correcting the bias would need more headroom than the link had.

accounting.note: delta_r counts the bits a decision moved from the link it should have taken to the link it actually took. It is a per-decision attribution, NOT end-to-end rerouted net traffic: later hops of the same packet can correct it. Every flip contributes one + and one -, so sum_r delta_r = 0 and sum_r |delta_r| counts each moved bit twice.

directional_bias.note: a flip needs both endpoint links; unpaired flips are dropped so that sum_r delta_r = 0 exactly

backlog_rebuild.definition: backlog = queued bits + in-service remaining bits (linear decay over [service_start, service_end])

trace_join.reason: load_calibration._project_decision drops the decision dst field, so reading dst from the decision row would silently collapse the (sat,dst) stream key to per-sat
trace_join.superseded_lens: per-sat grouping (Round-1 W/switch) is kept only as a documented cross-check in persistence.flip_runs_by_sat_only

binned_bias_runs.note: 0.5 s-bin view of the same |delta_r| bias: durations are QUANTIZED to the bin width and are NOT tau_error

error_runs_exact.definition: per-link runs of flip decisions wrongly pushed into the same link, joined only while consecutive decisions are <= 1 s apart; duration is t_last - t_first

flip_runs_by_sat_only.note: per-sat key (the Round-1 W/switch lens) - superseded: the decision projection drops dst, so a per-sat key is what the old numbers implicitly used; the (sat,dst) join above is authoritative

persistence.tau_error_definition: duration = t(last flip) - t(first flip) of a maximal run of consecutive flips with the same chosen direction inside one (sat,dst) stream; decision timestamps, no bin quantization

queue_relaxation.peak_floor_rule: peak backlog >= 2 service slots (1 slot = one packet in service)

tau_error_vs_relax.note: coverage: only error runs on a corridor link that has at least one relaxation episode can enter this table; see persistence.error_runs_exact.n_runs_with_relax for the covered count. descriptive split only: no fit, no significance claim. tau_relax is the per-link median tau_50 over that link's relaxation episodes (resolved at event timestamps); tau_error is the run duration at |delta| > 0.05*mu. E2E is measured on packets that entered the link queue inside the segment; the baseline is every packet that entered that link at any time in the run.

z_bins.epsilon_floor_rule: z_valid only keeps flips whose epsilon_r >= max(EPS_FLOOR, 1% of mu)

non_flip_decisions.note: no delta by definition -> no z; contrast row only
